thread.title: A rally in 10-year government bonds means one thing: the stock market is going nowhere fast

author: Mark DeCambre
title: A rally in 10-year government bonds means one thing: the stock market is going nowhere fast
text: A rally in the 10-year Treasury note, driving yields lower, late Tuesday is implying that investors are picking up long-dated bonds, perceived as havens, as the stock market attempts to register a second straight day of gains. The 10-year Treasury yield TMUBMUSD10Y, -2.82% hit a nadir around 2.79% during Tuesday's action, representing the lowest closing yield since Feb. 6, according to WSJ Market Data Group (based on 3 p.m. ET closes). Bond prices rise and yields fall. Bond buying comes even as the market has been digesting some $300 billion in issuance slated for this holiday-shortened week for the fixed-income market, with Good Friday marking a holiday for the market. More issuance should drive yields up. Meanwhile, the equity benchmarks were unraveling, notably the Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -2.97% was off by 2.7%, cutting deeply into the technology-laden index's 3.3% return on Monday. The S&P 500 index SPX, -1.82% was off 1.3% at 2,616, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -1.44% made up of 30 components, was down a more modest 1.3%, led by sharp slumps in shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, -2.73% and Microsoft Inc. MSFT, -4.48% Much of Monday's rise was attributed to a lessening of worries around trade conflicts between the U.S. and China, but Tuesday's trade suggests that investors are more eager to buy long-dated bond than make a definitive wager on another blockbuster day for technology shares and the broader stock market, considered risky, after the Dow's 670-point surge a day earlier.
